reviewComments.body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The sync worker fetches queued jobs using a simple select. In a multi-worker environment, multiple workers will fetch the same set of 'queued' jobs, leading to redundant execution and potential race conditions during upserts. A proper 'claim' mechanism (e.g., using a database-level lock or an atomic update to a 'running' status with a worker ID) is required for production readiness.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Similar to the sync worker, the webhook delivery worker lacks a concurrency control mechanism. Multiple instances will attempt to process the same due deliveries. Use an atomic 'update and return' pattern to ensure each delivery is processed by exactly one worker.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The Hono adapter uses a catch-all route to delegate to the internal router. However, `c.req.raw` is used directly without considering that the body might have already been consumed by Hono middleware (e.g., `hono/logger` or `hono/body-parser`). While `toMountedRequest` creates a new Request, if the original body stream is locked, this will fail. Ensure that the body is handled defensively or that this adapter is intended to be used without body-consuming middleware upstream.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The persistence sink logic executes the `transform` function twice for every item: once in `idempotencyKey` (via `createDbSink`) and once in the explicit `transform` call. If the transformation logic is computationally expensive or involves database lookups, this will significantly degrade sync performance. Refactor the sink interface or the runner to execute the transformation once per item.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Sync checkpoints are only persisted at the end of a successful sync run (which can span up to 50 pages). If a sync job fails or the process crashes on page 49, all progress from the previous 48 pages is lost. For durable and efficient syncs, checkpoints should be persisted after every page or after a small batch of pages.

![security-medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-medium-priority.svg) ![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Webhook idempotency check only verifies the existence of a 'verified' receipt for the given `idempotencyKey`. It does not verify that the `payloadHash` matches. This allows a different payload with a reused idempotency key to be incorrectly treated as a duplicate of a previously verified event. Include the payload hash in the idempotency lookup.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `listWebhookDeliveriesForRetry` method fetches all pending and failed deliveries into memory before filtering and sorting. In a production system with a high volume of webhooks or transient failures, this will lead to excessive memory consumption and slow worker performance. This filtering and sorting should be performed at the database level using SQL `WHERE` and `ORDER BY` clauses.

![security-medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/security-medium-priority.svg) ![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `validateEncryptionKey` function allows passphrases that are at least 32 characters long. However, it only checks for a diversity of 8 unique characters. A passphrase like 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaabbbbbbbb' would pass but is weak. Consider using a more robust entropy check or strictly requiring a 32-byte hex key for production environments.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin @plugfn/client to the current plugfn core version**

`@plugfn/client` declares `"plugfn": "0.0.1"`, but this commit sets the `plugfn` package itself to `0.1.0` (`plugfn/core/package.json`). With an exact version pin, consumers can resolve or install an older registry build (or fail if `0.0.1` is unavailable) instead of the newly introduced core API from this commit, which will break cross-package compatibility at install/runtime boundaries.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin @plugfn/providers to the current plugfn core version**

`@plugfn/providers` also hard-pins `"plugfn": "0.0.1"` while core is versioned to `0.1.0` in this same change. This creates the same dependency skew risk for provider package consumers: npm can resolve the wrong core version (or fail resolution), causing provider/runtime contract mismatches that are hard to debug after publish.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
